citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
All records of production associated with a batch of drug product are not maintained at least one (1) year after the expiration date.

citations.short: Complete test data included in records
citations.long: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations and assay necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards.

citations.short: Product flow through building is inadequate
citations.long: The flow of components, drug product containers, closures, labeling, in-process materials, and drug products though the building is not designed to prevent contamination.
Aseptic processing areas are deficient regarding the system for monitoring environmental conditions.

citations.short: Written procedures lacking for use of pesticides etc.
citations.long: Written procedures are lacking for the use of rodenticides, insecticides, fungicides, fumigating agents, and cleaning and sanitizing agents designed to prevent the contamination of equipment, components, drug product containers, closures, packaging, labeling materials, and drug products.

Written procedures for cleaning and maintenance fail to include maintenance and cleaning schedules, description in sufficient detail of methods, equipment and materials used, description in sufficient detail of the methods of disassembling and reassembling equipment as necessary to assure proper cleaning and maintenance, and instructions for removal or obliteration of previous batch identification.
Procedures for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment are deficient regarding maintenance and cleaning schedules, including, where appropriate, sanitizing schedules.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.
Written records of investigations into the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and follow-up.
Employees engaged in the manufacture of a drug product lack the training required to perform their assigned functions.
Protective apparel is not worn as necessary to protect drug products from contamination.
Written procedures for sanitation are not followed.
Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are not written.
Laboratory controls do not include a determination of conformance to written descriptions of sampling procedures for drug products.
The written stability testing program is not followed.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.

citations.short: Complete test data included in records
citations.long: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations and assay necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards.

citations.short: Contamination, chemical or physical change, deterioration
citations.long: An NDA-Field Alert Report was not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning significant chemical, physical, or other change or deterioration in a distributed drug product.
